prediction.beta: New mode in testing — predict BTC's 5-minute direction. Prices, settlement rule and taker fees follow polymarket.com.
prediction.title: BTC 5-minute prediction
prediction.targetTip: Chainlink 60-second time-weighted average price (TWAP) at the moment the round opened; this is Polymarket's price to beat. Settlement uses the 60-second TWAP at the close: at or above it is Up, below is Down.
prediction.upTip: Probability price: 50¢ = the market gives a 50% chance of going up. Higher price, stronger conviction.
prediction.downTip: Probability price: 50¢ = the market gives a 50% chance of going down. Higher price, stronger conviction.
prediction.estPayoutTip: Right prediction: every contract settles at $1. Payout = amount ÷ probability price; the fee is charged on top of the amount.
prediction.feeTip: Polymarket taker fee: shares × 7% × price × (1 − price). Most expensive at 50¢ (1.75¢ per share), cheaper toward the extremes.
prediction.estProceedsTip: What you receive at the current sell price, after fees.
prediction.mySharesTip: Contracts you hold; each is worth $1 if the prediction is right.

jev.title: Jev predictor
jev.intro: Jev bets on BTC's 5-minute up/down market like a player: every 15 seconds after the open it looks at the market and decides itself — when flat, buy UP, buy DOWN or pass; when holding, keep the bet or sell it. Code only works out the numbers for it, such as costs and a math estimate, and places the trades Jev decides on.
jev.archivedBanner: Viewing archived run {{n}}: it no longer bets, and its bets, decisions and scores stay as they ended.
jev.pnlLabel: PnL this run · settled bets, after fees
jev.scoreDetailsSub: How accurate is Jev's win chance? · {{n}} samples
jev.brierExplain: At every checkpoint the three chances of UP are checked against the result: UP counts as 1, DOWN as 0, and we average (chance − result)². 0 is perfect; 0.25 is what always guessing 50% gets.
jev.brierHow: Watch Jev: lower than Market means Jev reads the window better than the market; lower than Math means it beats the formula that only looks at the gap and the time left. The lowest in each row is orange.
jev.calibration: Calibration: does 70% come true 70% of the time?
jev.calibrationExplain: Jev's chances are split into five bands, and each band shows how often BTC actually finished UP. In the 60%–80% band, roughly seven in ten should have gone UP. The bar is the actual share, the tick is the band's average forecast; the closer the bar's end is to the tick, the better.
jev.guideAction: The first line is what actually happened this time (Buy UP / Buy DOWN / Sell / Hold / Stay out), how much was staked, the time, and how many seconds after the open.
jev.guideDecides: The second line is Jev's decision and its confidence: when flat it picks Buy UP / Buy DOWN / Pass, when holding it picks Hold / Sell. The "By the math" number after it is a reference: when flat, how much more each share of that side is worth than it costs (estimated win chance − ask − fee); when holding, how much more selling now gets per share than the estimate. What Jev sees uses the same formula with the estimate rounded to a whole percent, so the two can differ by half a cent. The decision is Jev's.
jev.guideUpChance: The three "Chance of UP" numbers estimate the same thing — will this window finish above the target price — in different ways:
jev.guideModel: From how far BTC is above the target, how many seconds are left, and how much BTC has been moving lately. Code writes its gap to both costs into what Jev sees; it does not decide for Jev.
jev.guideJev: Jev's own win chance: the same request also asks "will this settle UP?" and "will this settle DOWN?", and the number is the average of UP-wins and 1 − DOWN-wins. It is only scored, to see how well Jev reads the window; it does not drive trades.
jev.guideMkt: Derived from the UP and DOWN prices in the order book. With UP around 67¢ and DOWN around 35¢, the market thinks about 66% UP.
jev.guideFold: Routine stay-out / hold rows are folded; use "Show all" on the right of each window. Click any row to see Jev's answer to every question.
jev.guideLegacy: R1 and R2 are old versions: in R1 Jev picked the trade itself and judged whether the move still had legs; in R2 Jev only gave a win chance, code bet by comparing it with the asks, and code sold by the math price. Old runs are shown as they were.
jev.guideQuestionsTitle: What Jev is asked each time
jev.qEntryDesc: Asked when flat. What Jev sees spells out both sides' asks, their cost with the fee and the math estimate, and asks it to judge from the market whether the true chance is higher or lower than the estimate; Jev picks one of the three and gives each a probability.
jev.qExitDesc: Asked while holding. What Jev sees spells out which side it holds, how many shares, the average price, what selling gets per share after the fee, and what the math estimate says it is worth; Jev picks one of the two. With nobody bidding it is not asked and keeps holding.
jev.qWinsDesc: Asked alongside at every checkpoint, for scoring only. The same request asks it both ways: will the final-minute average end at or above the opening average (UP wins), and will it end below (DOWN wins). Jev answers with probabilities; averaging the two framings cancels out any lean from the wording.
jev.guideBuy: Code follows Jev's buy only when that pick has {{act}} or more (no less than all other picks combined), ${{stake}} a bet. Code only blocks mechanical problems: nobody selling that side, or a wallet that cannot afford a bet. When the wallet cannot afford a bet it stops itself until a new run.
jev.guideSell: While holding, code sells when Jev picks Sell with {{act}} or more and more than Hold; with nobody bidding it has to keep holding. After selling it can buy again in the same window.
jev.guideFill: Fills have a delay like a real order: {{delay}}s after Jev decides, code checks the book again and fills at that price if it is no more than {{tol}}¢ worse than what Jev saw; otherwise the trade is missed.

notice.NO_QUOTE_BOTH: Blocked: nobody is selling either side
notice.ASK_RANGE: Blocked: {{side}} ask {{ask}}¢ was outside the buy range at the time
notice.NOT_CHEAP: Blocked: {{side}} is not cheap enough by the math
notice.EXPENSIVE: Blocked: {{side}}'s ask is above the math fair price
notice.NO_BALANCE: Blocked: the game wallet cannot afford a bet
notice.STALE_BOOK: The order book has not updated for {{sec}}s; Jev was not asked
notice.STALE_BOOK_NONE: No order book updates on record; Jev was not asked
notice.STALE_CHAINLINK: The Chainlink price has not updated for {{sec}}s (an outage on Polymarket's side); Jev was not asked
notice.STALE_WHILE_ASKING: The order book froze; not executed
notice.MISSED: Missed: while waiting to fill, the {{side}} ask moved from {{from}}¢ to {{to}}¢
notice.MISSED_GONE: Missed: while waiting to fill, nobody was selling {{side}} any more (the ask was {{from}}¢)
notice.MISSED_SELL: Not sold: while waiting to fill, the bid moved from {{from}}¢ to {{to}}¢
notice.MISSED_SELL_GONE: Not sold: while waiting to fill, nobody was bidding any more (the bid was {{from}}¢)
notice.FILLED_AT: Expected to buy at {{from}}¢, filled at {{to}}¢
notice.SOLD_AT: Expected to sell at {{from}}¢, sold at {{to}}¢
